Spiced Tea

Served at: Second Sunday of Advent

Serves 4Prep 5 minCook 10 min

Spiced Tea is a warm, aromatic beverage traditionally enjoyed on the Second Sunday of Advent, a time of anticipation and reflection leading up to Christmas. This comforting drink combines black tea with festive spices, evoking the cozy spirit of the holiday season.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (960 ml) water
  • 4 black tea bags
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 4 whole cloves
  • 4 whole cardamom pods, lightly crushed
  • 1 star anise
  • 1-inch (2.5 cm) piece fresh ginger, sliced
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) honey or to taste
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk or cream, optional

Method

  1. Bring the water to a boil in a medium saucepan.
  2. Add the cinnamon stick, cloves, cardamom pods, star anise, and sliced ginger to the boiling water.
  3. Reduce heat and simmer the spices for 5 minutes to release their flavors.
  4. Add the black tea bags to the spiced water and steep for 3 to 5 minutes, depending on desired strength.
  5. Remove the tea bags and strain the tea to remove the spices.
  6. Stir in honey to sweeten, adjusting to taste.
  7. If desired, add milk or cream and heat gently until warm.
  8. Serve the spiced tea hot in mugs.

Tips

  • For a caffeine-free version, substitute black tea with rooibos or herbal tea.
  • Adjust the spice quantities to suit your taste; more ginger for a spicier kick, or extra cinnamon for warmth.
  • Add a slice of orange or a splash of vanilla extract for a unique twist.
